raw_response:
Eh, let me think this through. I've been farming these 5.5 mu for thirty-five years — same wheat-maize rotation as everyone in our village. My son works in the city, sends some money home, so mostly it's me and my husband in the field. At our age we can't do everything by hand anymore, so we hire the combine at harvest, 60 yuan per mu, worth every fen.

The wheat is already in the ground — I planted it back in October, around the 12th after the autumn rain softened the soil. I always buy Jimai seed from the supply store in town, maybe 15 kg per mu because the soil was a bit dry that week. Before plowing I spread 50 kg of that 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu. Most people here do the same. Now the wheat is at jointing — I'll topdress about 15 kg of urea before the next irrigation so the water carries it down. Normally two irrigations gets us through — jointing and heading — but if spring stays dry I'll do a third. I'm watching for aphids; last year they were bad, so I'll spray once at heading with a pyrethroid plus a bit of fungicide for powdery mildew. If nothing goes wrong I expect around 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 430.

For maize, the turnaround after wheat is only five or six days. I hire Wang's son with his no-till planter — 30 yuan per mu, he drops seed and starter fertilizer in one pass. I use Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the store has that year. Then at the big-leaf stage I topdress maybe 20 kg urea per mu. If July rains come normal I don't irrigate; if it's dry I'll do one. One spray for armyworm and corn borer. I usually get about 500 kg per mu — 510 last year.

Money is tight like always. I don't want to borrow at my age, so I keep the inputs at what I know works. Fertilizer has gone up again this year, but I won't cut back — if I skimp on fertilizer the yield drops too much and I lose more than I save. Better to put down what I always put down.
